comparisons.evidence: Q sustains more distinct mechanisms, including environmental certification ("Personal Technical Rider"), regional redundancy ("Duplicate Life Modules"), preventive maintenance, reversible commitments, asynchronous physical play, load shedding and burstwork. P is also broad, but several ideas cluster around cross-border administration, housing exchange and portable care.

Q moves further beyond standard retiree services with ideas such as commitments that "expire unless renewed," a room-scale "cognitive ‘home state’," and distance used "as a storytelling mechanic." P has strong departures such as "Care-Hours Futures," but its leading pick, "Jurisdiction Autopilot," remains closer to familiar compliance software.

Q explicitly assigns operational rules to candidates—"Positive handoff," "Preventive maintenance," "Reversible intervention"—and makes finalists depend on them. For example, the relay requires acknowledgement and a standardized handoff packet, while commitments decay by default. P derives credible concepts from "migratory-bird ecology" and "financial derivatives," but some borrowing is looser and less visibly carried into the final product mechanics.

Q's "Personal Technical Rider" directly targets a frequent, retiree-specific problem, has an institutional payer—"Property operators pay to qualify"—and can be tested with a spreadsheet. P's "Jurisdiction Autopilot" is credible, but its claim of a "fast software MVP" understates the legal-liability and rule-maintenance difficulty that P itself identifies.

Q converts assumptions into concrete falsification tests, such as "Kill the idea if clarification cycles erase the time-zone advantage" and testing whether ledger entries "become stale without heavy prompting." P names real risks—"provider insolvency," "clinical liability," "hostile incumbent contracts"—but generally stops short of specifying decisive observations that would invalidate an idea.

Both articulate sharp, mechanism-level insights. P observes that users may pay "to avoid creating a legal obligation" and that money does not ensure "a trusted person will appear." Q reframes time-zone difference as "inventory" and argues that mobility may be limited by "the residue left behind by every previous place." Neither set relies mainly on platitudes.

note: The biggest difference is that Q turns its borrowed rules into explicit product dependencies and falsifiable tests, whereas P offers broader venture concepts with stronger portfolio and business-model framing.
